scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A refund claim
scenes.caption: A buyer promises Dev’s aunt a refund. The buyer sends a pretend QR card and says she must scan it and enter her UPI PIN to receive money. Dev reads the paper screen.
scenes.dialogue: Read the action on the screen.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Follow the arrow
scenes.caption: The prepared screen says Pay merchant: sixty rupees. Its arrow points from the aunt’s wallet toward the merchant. The buyer’s message says receive, but the displayed action says pay. The class traces that difference without opening any banking application.
scenes.dialogue: Words in a chat do not reverse money.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: The PIN’s purpose
scenes.caption: A UPI PIN authorises payment actions; receiving money does not require entering it. A QR image is not evidence that a refund is genuine. Dev does not scan, enter a PIN or test the claim with a small amount.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: The decision point
scenes.caption: The buyer becomes impatient and promises an instant return. Dev can encourage his aunt to approve, send her PIN to the buyer, or pause and cancel this request. Choose the response supported by the displayed direction and the PIN’s purpose.
scenes.dialogue: The responsible adult handles the account.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: A clear explanation
scenes.caption: Dev explains that the screen would send money outward. His aunt cancels and checks the original transaction through her already known provider route. They keep an imaginary direction note; the lesson does not ask children to operate anyone’s account.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: A new label
scenes.caption: In the lab, a changed request calls itself a scholarship deposit, yet the screen still says Pay. Trace the new arrows, count outgoing amounts and explain why a kinder label cannot change the action.
